ISC Practical Manual Guide
OBJECT (Experiment 1):
C-10: 1.85 g of KMnO₄ per litre. C-11: 22 g of hydrated ammonium iron(II) sulphate, (NH₄)₂SO₄·FeSO₄·xH₂O, per litre. Find the molarities, the molecular mass and x.
Burette: 25 mL, least count 0.1 mL · Pipette: 20 mL · C-12: 20 mL dilute H₂SO₄ per titration
TITRATION 1 — STEP 1
Rinse the burette
Reading a burette (30-second idea)
KMnO₄ is so dark that you cannot see the bottom of its curved surface, so you read the top edge of the liquid (the upper meniscus). Keep your eye level with it: then the front and back of the ring mark there look like one straight line. From above or below the ring looks like an oval and the reading comes out wrong (parallax).
Concordant readings (what your teacher asks for)
One titration can go slightly wrong, so you repeat it. Readings are concordant when they agree within 0.1 mL (for example 19.2 and 19.2, or 19.2 and 19.3). The titre value used in the calculation is the mean of the concordant readings. A first rough run, or any reading that does not agree, is not used.
Equation (n₁ : n₂ = 2 : 10)
2MnO₄⁻ + 10Fe²⁺ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10Fe³⁺ + 8H₂O
M₁V₁ / M₂V₂ = n₁ / n₂ = 2 / 10. KMnO₄ is its own indicator: the first drop it is not used up turns the flask light pink.
